utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Case Number IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Brdjanin, can you follow in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you. Appearances, Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Julian Nicholls with Denise Gustin and Joanna Korner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you and good afternoon. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Defence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Defence, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm John Ackerman --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I didn't recognise you, Mr. Ackerman. That's the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I have been to a mad dentist since I last saw you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm John Ackerman and I'm with David Cunningham and Aleksandar Vujic, even though I know I don't look like him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And good afternoon to you. I don't want to impose on you, Mr. Ackerman. I see that you have a really swollen face. Are you in a position to follow the proceedings or not? I know that it's the cross-examination, but...

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I wouldn't be here if I couldn't be here. I'm fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm being courteous to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I understand that, and I appreciate it. I think I'll be all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you have a problem, let me know. Any preliminaries?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just two matters. Mr. Ackerman was good enough to tell me today just before we sat that the documents that I asked for the provenance of come -- came from a Mr. Glogovac who took over the agency when Mr. Bojinovic left. Your Honour, I'm prepared to accept that, and I withdraw my objection at the moment. I withdraw my objection to the admission of those documents. Mr. Glogovac appears in the papers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So I'm prepared to accept that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The witness said that the organisation was replaced, not taken over, but -- his place wasn't taken over. He said that it was replaced by the refugee or --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let me put it this way, I don't think at this stage of the game anyhow we ought to start delving into that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it may well be THAT at a later stage we may have to revisit this topic, but at this moment I withdraw my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wasn't using precise language when I said "taken over" after -- that was just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Some kind of a successor who turned over the documents. That's the best I can say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the only other matter is if we have time this afternoon I would like to address Your Honours very briefly on part of the judgement that you gave, the written judgement on the Rule 98 decisions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was reminded today to remind you when to expect the revised indictment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm so sorry, Your Honour. Of course, we had it ready to go -- Your Honour, we can have it filed by the end of the week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So let's start with the witness, Madam Usher. Yes, exactly. The way it is, I am not seeing Mr. Ackerman, I'm not seeing the accused, I'm not seeing Mr. Cunningham. Mr. Billow now is used to being hidden from the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: He says it's easier to play video games that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, Mr. Vidic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are going to continue with your testimony on cross-examination. Just reminding you for formality sake that you are testifying under oath on the basis of your solemn declaration of yesterday. So please, take a seat, a chair, and let's proceed. Mr. Nicholls. I have to repeat presumably. Were you receiving interpretation or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I haven't received any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We are going to proceed with your cross-examination and reminding you that you are testifying on the basis of your solemn declaration of yesterday which you are not going to repeat today because you don't need to. All right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could the ELMO be moved somehow so that I can -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to try to cover several topics today. I'll try to make them clear. If both of us can try to be as clear and concise as possible, we can finish today.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I looked at what we have been talking about yesterday and have just a couple follow-up questions to you. You talked about with Mr. Ackerman how your interest in regionalisation, your interest in forming a new multiethnic body and your discussions on this topic led to - one way or another - to the formation of the associations of communities, first the ZOBK, Z-O-B-K, and then the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you were -- at that time, I think you said that you were getting pretty excited about these new political developments in the early 1990s and wanted to be a part of it. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You said you talked about it with several people. I think you said Mr. Brdjanin was one of the people you discussed these new associations with, this new regionalisation process.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: He was also a strong supporter of this regionalisation process, as you were yourself. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, I just want to very quickly -- you don't need to tell me the dates. I just want to be clear on all the different positions you held. At one point you were president of the Prnjavor SDS. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You have been a member of the SDS main board?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You were -- and we saw this on P95 yesterday, the document where you were addressing the ARK Assembly about the incident with Veljko Milankovic. You were vice-chairman of the executive council of the ARK. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Formally, yes, but not in any active sense of the word.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You were a deputy in the association of municipalities of the Bosnian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was a deputy to the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. You were a deputy later on in the Assembly of the Serbian People, or at some point?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you were also a deputy in the Republika Srpska Assembly?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to go back to and finish talking about Veljko Milankovic. We talked yesterday, you talked with Mr. Ackerman and with myself about the 14th of December 1991 ARK Assembly decision not to support -- in fact, to support the actions to arrest Veljko Milankovic. Correct? Do you remember us talking about that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to now play you a tape recording of a conversation conducted on the 26th of November 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, just out of an abundance of caution based upon our objection to all of these intercepts, I want to make sure that I make a formal objection to the use of this as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This will be P2710. This is in Sanction. I've never tried this before.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think, sir, you're going to hear yourself talking to Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't know if the interpreters can follow this this quickly. We've got the transcript. Maybe we can just have him listen to the tape and go along. It should be coming up on Sanction as we go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's all right for, I suppose, the three of us, because we have the transcript. We don't need to hear the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The screen should be synchronised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can also read it. It's easier on our eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I was thinking it sounded impossible for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I don't exclude that someone might prefer to listen to it or to -- so that one can check. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's no problem with the interpreter remaining silent. It's on the screen. It's going out --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know it's on the screen. And probably the interpreter is reading from the screen anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It would be nice to start over at the beginning, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's what we're going to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Listen to this whole recording, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me stop it now and ask you a couple questions. Do you recognise your voice on that tape recording, sir?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember having this conversation with Radovan Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'd forgotten about it, but now I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Let me just ask you where we've got to at this point. You stated: "Well, I'm calling you. Well, we agreed, I, Vojo and Vukic, you know." What were you calling Dr. Karadzic about? This was on 26th of November 1991.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I called him to justify myself for what I had not been able to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, you said, and we've already heard this: "We have everything, we accomplished everything, and today we're pursuing something" and so on. So what had you accomplished and what had you not been able to do?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are no secrets involved. That much is clear. Mr. Rankic, he and his wife, used to work for a company, a company that printed propaganda material. They would agree on deals with the commercial offices of the company concerning the calendars for the coming year, and the rest of the propaganda material. They charged their fees, and this was done by Mr. Veselinovic's [phoen] company. Let me see if I can remember the name. They were, I believe, in charge of actually printing the material. Probably though, some of the party activities were funded from the same source. This had nothing to do with Krajina, therefore, and my conversation with Mr. Karadzic was a private one. It was not on behalf of Krajina that I talked to Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. What was Mr. Rankic's first name?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rankic -- truth to tell, I can't remember. I know that it was he and his wife. They drove a car, and they sold books. Books and leaflets.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The question was whether you remembered his first name. When you say we agreed --

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry, I cut you off. When you say: "Well, we agreed, I, Vojo and Vukic," that's Vojo Kupresanin, correct? And Dr. Vukic?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What sort of propaganda was this? You used that word.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was not propaganda on behalf of the party. This was a commercial activity, a commercial printing activity. Certain companies would order propaganda material for themselves. I made a private promise to find commercial people in Prnjavor Municipality, because I was myself involved in the economy, I had plenty of contacts, and I was myself owner of a company. I promised to put him in touch with certain companies and certain people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: However --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think you've cleared that up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we play the tape. We have no sound, Your Honour. Maybe if you start it from the beginning again. It wasn't very far, if that works. I apologise, Your Honours. I don't know why the sound has stopped working on Sanction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not playing, anyway. It's --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: She stopped it playing because there was no sound. Ms. Gustin has stopped it because there was no sound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think this is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's not it, Your Honour. I propose, Your Honours, to give a copy of the transcript to the witness in his language and we will go ahead without playing the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I suggest you do is, Ms. Gustin, cancel it. Exit from this particular exhibit. And then go into it again. First exit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember that portion of the conversation?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not so well, but...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman. Sorry, I apologise --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's a problem. If you saw the transcript as it was coming off the LiveNote, that last bit said it was Karadzic that was speaking. If you look at the transcript, it says that it was Vidic that was speaking, in both versions. And I think the transcript is accurate, and what was on the LiveNote is inaccurate because I think it was -- it was Mr. Vidic who said they should really be disciplined. That's absolutely clear. And then he's the one that's saying "hello, hello, hello, hello." I believe that's the reality as opposed to what we saw on the LiveNote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was following on the proposed exhibit transcript, and not on the screen. But I take your word for it that is what has appeared on the monitor. If that is the case, I would like confirmation from you, Mr. Nicholls, that what Mr. Ackerman is saying stating is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was looking at my paper version as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was following the paper version as well, so I'm not in a position to say which one of this is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I requested a draft translation of this. I requested a translation of this. There may have been one from the day before that was put on here. I think the only thing to do is to play the tape and ask the witness. But we can hear it on the tape. It should be apparent. They have distinct voices.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The voices I was listening to because I still had this, the earphones on. But I suppose you can play the last part and have the witness confirm whether it's him or Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We can try.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He might know right now, Your Honour. He was listening to it as it was going forward. You might just ask the witness righted now who the last speaker was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who was saying "hello, hello, hello, hello"? Was it you or Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was Mr. Karadzic. He spoke at the end of the tape --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's listen to the last part because we have a confusion here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, we have to go further up, further back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I think, Mr. Ackerman, you were wrong, I am wrong. The paper version is wrong. I think it's Mr. Karadzic who is saying those words, the last four lines or five lines. Correct? Not you. 20

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And Your Honour, while we're here, I'll admit the tape, and that will be 2710A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because I lost my pen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry that took so long, Your Honours. The next time we'll just bring in a tape recorder. I have several at home, and it would have worked just as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're not finish with this because the transcript can't be admitted because of its inaccuracy. It needs to be fixed. The transcript is clearly wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll submit a revised transcript. That's the only thing I've noticed that's wrong, and we can fix that and put in a final translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. In the meantime, what's your question to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now you've heard it twice. Clearly you were talking to Karadzic about the arrest of Milankovic which had happened just a short time earlier. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How well did you know Karadzic at this point?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not sufficiently. Only from the political meetings. I saw him for the first time a year or so before that. It was in July 1990. That was the first time that I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You had talked to him on the phone person to person before this though, hadn't you? This wasn't the first time you had a telephone call directly to Dr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the second -- I think I spoke to him only three times over the phone. It was on my initiative.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now, he asked you about who's still being held, and you tell him that Veljko Milankovic is being held and somebody with the nickname Crni. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Why -- briefly, why were all the rest of those men released so quickly?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I called Karadzic to justify myself for what I had failed to do for Mr. Rankic because I had promised to do so as a private citizen, not in any official capacity. I didn't do it. I felt uncomfortable going there and intervening on behalf of a company to get a job. And I was opposed to the sale of these books because I personally did not like them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, you're not answering my question at all. Why were all of these 30 or so men in this criminal group released other than the two people we've talked about, Milankovic and Crni?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why they had been released.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You tell Karadzic that you went and talked to the judge about this incident, the civilian judge. Why did you do that?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Due to a coincidence, one of the judges was my wife. But she was not in charge of the case. She only had information about it. I didn't say anything else. I just told Mr. Karadzic what I had heard, and I had zero influence at that time. He was asking about this group over the phone. He was asking me --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay, you've gone --

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- But I --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: He asked you what is being ascribed to them, what are they -- what is being ascribed to these men? What is it said they have done "this time"? And you say: "They have been released. They have been a little humiliated, but that was done in a stupid way, you know. It could have been done differently. This is, well, our opinion." How should that release have been done differently and what's your opinion about that? You said the humiliation was done in a stupid way.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I still think. If somebody is beaten in the course of an arrest and hit with a rifle and so on, there was an easier way to do so, easier way to arrest them without bringing the lives of other citizens in danger.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And when these men were arrested, they had stolen property, Karadzic calls it loot, with them. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what it is that they had. I was just telling Mr. Karadzic what I had heard. So I did not have any access to investigative organs. I didn't have any access to the institutions in the executive --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm only asking you to tell us what you knew. You were discussing this with Dr. Karadzic, and you said that this so-called loot was collected from apartments. And then you said the question was what to do with it, and that depended on, if I read this correctly, where it came from. Now, are there you talking about matters whether this property was taken from Serbs or non-Serbs? Is that the distinction you're making?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Definitely not. I always felt that criminal offences committed against all citizens are the same, regardless of their ethnic background. And those people who know me can vouch for that. Many people would be able to confirm this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So tell me what did you mean when you said words to the effect of "Where did it come from? That is the question."?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I heard was that during the arrest, in their apartments, there were certain items that were found there, furniture, TV sets, things like that. But the police did not have any evidence indicating that these items had been stolen. In the course of the investigation, they were probably trying to ascertain what had been stolen and what hadn't been stolen and where these items had come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now there's a conversation between you and Karadzic that shows the tension we were talking about yesterday. Karadzic tells you that what he heard from reporters, that the way Milankovic's unit fight is incredible, and you say words to the effect of: "It's incredible. They are real fighters. No doubt about that." Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then you say: "And regarding this action and work, they were really good with that in the last, well, two to three months." Now, tell me what the action and work these men who we agreed yesterday were armed paramilitary criminals were really good at and what they were doing so well for the last two to three months that you praised them for?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is strange. There's something strange about this speech. I didn't mean actions. I wanted to say that they had been doing things before, and then they were threatened. And after that, they were calm for a while. They did not cause any trouble. But they were arrested all the same. What I meant had more to do with this. The outrageous things that they did before, they were really impossible when they came back from Krajina in Croatia. And since at that time there was a cease-fire in effect, it had been signed in Krajina at that time, probably somebody who was their commander probably advised them to calm down a bit. And I was not quite sure whether Karadzic himself was behind it, and that is why I was really very careful in the conversation. I was letting him say things, and then I would agree to what he said. You can see that from the conversation. I was not in a position to influence anything. And I was also on very, very bad terms with this group from day one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm not asking about your potential influence. Just try to answer the question. You're the one who offered this comment, this is in response to a question. After talking about how they were great fighters, how everything was good in the last two to three months, are you sure you weren't talking about the takeover of the Kozara transmitter and their other paramilitary activities?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I was referring to newspaper articles and TV broadcasts where there were reports about them as fighters, that they are well trained and things like that. The newspapers were full of articles such as this to that effect. And I could not oppose Mr. Karadzic because I was not quite sure on what terms he was with these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now, again, yesterday with Mr. Ackerman and with myself, you talked about the report you made to the assembly and the conclusion signed by Mr. Kupresanin supporting the arrest of Veljko Milankovic's paramilitary. I'd like you to look now at P2707.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I have a highlighted copy, which may make it quicker.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is a Glas article from the 11th of April 1992 with the headline "Anatomy of betrayal, walking on Serbian thorns." It concerns the -- it celebrates the fact that Veljko Milankovic is not going to be prosecuted for his crimes in Prnjavor. I'd like you to read the first highlighted portion I've provided for you which should start: "The walk on thorns by the fighters of Veljko Milankovic's unit began on the early morning of 14 November..." Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's talking about -- we're talking about the same arrest of Veljko Milankovic that you were talking about with Mr. Karadzic on the telephone. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know because there were -- Mr. Milankovic was arrested on several occasions, so I don't know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no idea how this could be the same one if the newspaper report is April of 1991 and the conversation is November of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: But still we're six months apart. I doubt it's the same arrest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think we have heard of more than one particular arrest of Milankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He was arrested at least twice, Your Honour, maybe three times. But certainly twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You were talking to Dr. Karadzic on the 26th of November. This is talking about an arrest on the 14th of November. I understand that this article was in the second -- another year. In any event, how many times are you aware of that he was arrested with 33 members of his unit in Prnjavor?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. I was incorrect. It is talking about the same. Obviously now that I pay attention to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll move on to my next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like you to skip to the second highlighted portion. This is Veljko Milankovic speaking. This is on page 4 of the English. "Although this is not the time for disputes among Serbs, I must say something. We were a unit of the Autonomous Region of the Bosnian Krajina. The president of the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina Vojo Kupresanin and the Prime Minister Andjelko Grahovac, as well as the members of the government and leadership of the Banja Luka SDS were fully informed about all our operations. Actually, we took part in operations at the order of the leadership of the Autonomous Region of Bosnian Krajina. That was the case when we seized a repeater on Mount Kozara and made it possible for Bosnian Krajina to watch Belgrade television broadcasts." Is that what it says in your version?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm sorry. Do you mean is it written here in this version?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's what you've just read in your language. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree with what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's not the question. I'm just trying to make sure we're on the same page that you just read.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm just trying to make sure that we're on the same page, we've read the same paragraph. The paragraph that I've just read to you, that's been translated to you, that's what it says in your version. Correct? You need to answer verbally.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read it, and yes, I understood what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me move on to P2577. I will be asking you a question about this document. This is -- this will be another Glas article from 28th of April 1992, two weeks later. This article is talking about a 27th of April extraordinary session of the Bosnian Krajina AR Assembly held in the afternoon, 1992. Did you attend that session?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I cannot state with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, you've heard about this session, haven't you? This was a pretty important one. Take a look at the first two paragraphs of the article and let me know when you've read them. This was a session with a great deal of concern about the possible withdrawal of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, now that you've read that, do you remember whether you attended the session or not?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know about this topic, but I cannot say whether I was present or not because I skipped quite a few of those sessions, especially the emergency or extraordinary ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, were you ever at a session which was addressed by Veljko Milankovic? If you look down at paragraph 5, you'll see that he spoke at this session.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I know that I was not there when he spoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, on page 2 of the English, "Veljko Milankovic's speech" - he's called the commander of the volunteers from Prnjavor - "attracted particular attention during the debate. He called for reason and asked for actions not just decisions and constant meetings." And Veljko Milankovic talks about the Banja Luka Corps and giving them some time. Does that seem odd to you, this thug, criminal, paramilitary leader who had been arrested and condemned by a resolution of the same assembly is now addressing it?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know what date are we talking about. Was it in April?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Look at the headline of the article. Yes.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at that time, I did not attend the sessions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That wasn't the question. If you don't want to answer that question, I'll let you not answer it. Dragan Djuric was --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure he's not -- he's refusing to answer the question. He may not understand it. I don't think he doesn't want to answer the question. So I ask that he be given an opportunity to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's fine with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's cut this. I mean, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think it's pretty obvious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just ask him again. I mean, it's...

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Don't you find it strange that this same assembly which heard your report and condemned Veljko Milankovic, approved of his arrest, is now having him there as a speaker?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if it is true, then it really is strange.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Dragan Djuric was the president of the SDS from Prnjavor April 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think -- I think -- sorry. Dragan Djuric was the one who replaced him. No?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Dragan Djuric stated that coordination between the Tuzla and Banja Luka Corps in that area, speaking of Derventa, was nonexistent and openly called for Veljko Milankovic to be named commander of the Defence for the Serbian Municipality of Derventa. Does that not indicate full support for Veljko Milankovic and his unit from the SDS in Derventa in Prnjavor?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. If this statement is --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's more than possible?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: He's arrested, the charges are dropped, he's released, he's invited to speak at the assembly and they proposed to make him a commander of a Serbian municipality's defence. That's support, isn't it, from the party?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I just want to make sure the record is clear that we have objected to these kinds of newspaper reports. There's no indication that this is an accurate report of what went on at that meeting. And so every question I think that's being asked should start with the presumption that this report is accurate because it may not be. We know that Milankovic and the editor of Glas were buddies. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is a totally improper objection. The Chamber can judge the weight --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not an objection. It's putting on the record his general objection with regard to newspaper articles.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Correct, but it was going into comment which is what I object to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah. The witness wasn't present at this meeting in any case, according to what he said. But let's proceed. Your questions are perfectly valid, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have every right to base yourself on what appears to be a report in a newspaper, the authenticity of which --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to intervene at this stage because I'm really getting tired of these objections about newspapers. Your Honours are aware that there's a witness who faithfully recorded in his diary all the matters that these records refer to. So it's no good Mr. Ackerman standing up each time he doesn't like what an article has said. Newspaper articles are, per se, inaccurate. As Mr. Nicholls has rightly said, it is for Your Honours to judge the weight, looking at all the evidence. I do think that these objections particularly in front of witnesses who hear them are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand, Ms. Korner, you're perfectly right, but I... Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: There's no witness who faithfully recorded everything in his diary. I think he was a drunk who unfaithfully recorded things and made up a lot of stuff. So there's no evidence that that man is a reliable witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No further --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And I have attacked him in that regard and I will continue to do so, to say that this is some special witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, no further comments like that in front of a witness, please. You know what the Rules are. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: May I make one more objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It has been the rule that the person handling the witness is the person who makes the objections. Ms. Korner is now starting both with the last witness and now with this witness, making objections while she is not responsible for the witness. We had a rule that the person responsible for the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, you are right as well, yes. Yes, he's right, Ms. Korner. So next time, you make the objection, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Looking further down in this article --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just one moment, Your Honour. Well, Mr. Ackerman almost succeeded in stopping you from answering the question. He's arrested --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I really object to that. That is an absolute, unfair attack on me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman. I'll protect you, Mr. Ackerman. Yes, Mr. Nicholls, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you have a problem with repeating the question, I will find it for you and --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I have found it with Ms. Gustin's help. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Repeat the question and the witness will answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Talking about Veljko Milankovic, the question was he's arrested, the charges are dropped. He's released and he's proposed to be made commander of a Serbian Defence of a Serbian municipality. That's support, isn't it, support from the party? It's more than just possible that he received the support?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to have to object because there's no factual basis for that question at all. One person, one person, Dragan Djuric makes that request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, please. Please. Answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Let me just make my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You made your objection and the objection is taken and the witness will answer the question. Look at the head of this document, and you know what this meeting was supposed to be about.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I do want to get my objection clear in the record, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The article says that Dragan Djuric made that recommendation, not that the party did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls. Mr. Vidic, please answer the question. And the question is for the umpteenth time, it's being suggested to you to agree that the SDS was supporting now Veljko Milankovic. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not entirely certain because not everyone supported that. There were some people who liked him, in particular. And one of these was also a man to whom a reference is being made here. Now, as to whether he was going to become a commander or anything, it was down to the military to make that decision because by that time everything had been placed under their command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's fine. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: But I think you'd agree with me that not just anybody off the street of no importance came in and addressed the ARK Assembly at these type of extraordinary, important meetings. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a bit ridiculous, but the Autonomous Region of Krajina could be many things at once. I'll give you my own example --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't think you understood my question. At an extraordinary session of the Bosnian Krajina regional assembly, not just anybody was going to come in and address the assembly on defence issues. Isn't that right? It's a simple question.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was perfectly possible for anyone to come in and address, and that is the God honest truth. That really is the truth. It was chaos, and it was precisely for that reason and for the way in which the whole thing functioned that I refused to take any further part in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. When -- let's go to P1532.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, this is a videotape. I'm not sure it it has been keyed up. It's in evidence. If possible, I think it may be quicker for me just to put questions based on the transcript, which is in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, do you agree to that, or do you object?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I object to questions being put until the witness has a chance to see what he is being questioned about, whether he sees the video or reads the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- That also has its importance, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right, we can play the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We can stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't like music, I take it, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, if we had more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, you can see that this is an interview of Vojo Kupresanin on the anniversary - we haven't played the beginning - discussing the takeover of Kozara transmitter. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And it speaks about how the historical decision was made three years ago to take over the relay, and it asks how and when did you get the idea to take over the relay. That's what the reporter has asked. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Mr. Kupresanin states: "We knew even back then that a state cannot be a state without its radio, TV, and other media, and without its currency. We, in the assembly of the former Bosnia and Herzegovina, knew that nothing could be achieved with the Muslims and Croats, the anti-Serbian coalition, and we were happy to part ways with them. We began the parting with the Autonomous Region and continued with the takeover of the relay." That's what Vojo Kupresanin said taking over the relay was all about. Correct? That's what he said. That's the question.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Does this sounds like he's talking about some kind of voluntary, economic chamber of commerce?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say that Mr. Vojo, he wasn't clear about many things. He didn't know what power meant. He didn't know what association meant. He was fond of making statements --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop, stop.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Answer the question. Does that sound like the organisation, the association he's describing, is some kind of benign, voluntary, economic association? That's very simple. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite obviously he sees it as some form of government, power, but in reality, it was nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So you agree that what he was speaking about sounds like an association with power, a type of government. That's what you just said. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And he says: "We began the parting from the Muslims and the Croats with the autonomous region." That's what regionalisation was really all about, wasn't it, the forced separation of the ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. The view of Mr. Kupresanin after January and February of 1992, after the Assembly of the Serbian People had adopted certain provisions, you can see from the statute of the Autonomous Region of Krajina that it had been envisaged as an association of municipalities using the provisions of the constitution of the former state. The transmitter belonged to the association of municipalities. There was no need to make any announcements about a violent takeover of the transmitter. It was a futile exercise in power. Someone was flexing their muscles.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Someone was flexing their muscles. We can talk about the statute later, and we will. I think you'd agree that there's nothing in the statute which authorises the use of paramilitary forces; yet, that happened. You need to speak up. I heard him say yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I heard him say yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's not on the shorthand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, I know. I agree with you, Ms. Korner. That's why I'm saying I heard him say yes. Because it's not -- doesn't show on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: He said yes to that last question, correct? I heard you -- Can you repeat your answer, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the answer -- question, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Someone was flexing their muscles. That's what you said. We can talk about the statute later, and we will. I guarantee that. I think you'd agree that there's nothing in the statute which authorises the use of paramilitary forces; yet, that happened. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to play the tape a little bit more. I'm just going to let it play, because I don't want to try skipping around at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We can stop now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Grahovac talks about meeting with Milankovic's men in 1991 at this restaurant to - he disagrees with you - to take over -- because of the necessity of taking over the transmitter by force. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I've understood your question. Who exactly does it refer to? Can you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You heard Mr. Grahovac speaking on the tape in response to the questions from the reporter about the significance of the Evropa restaurant, that's where a meeting took place, a fateful meeting in 1991 with the Wolves of Vucak with Veljko Milankovic in order to plan the military takeover of the transmitter. That's what he said. Right? That's the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If I read the witness well, there is a problem with the interpretation. Are you receiving interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It stopped for a brief moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm wondering if we might break a few minutes earlier because there's something I want to bring to your attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll stop here with the testimony. We'll go back to your question in a minute, Mr. Nicholls. We're going to have a break, and we'll continue in about 25 minutes' time. Usher, no, we are staying here. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the first matter, we need to go to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just want the record to show that the direct examination of this witness started at 9.22 yesterday morning and ended at 11.30, and there was an intervening 25-minute break. I took an hour and 15 minutes. The Prosecution has now used three hours and 35 minutes of cross-examination. I want to read from a transcript of 21 July 2003.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Baruch, how much time do you think your require for your witness, your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I can't tell you that, Your Honour, because I had to listen to what he said before I could plan it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need to know as well. I mean, it's...

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: But I think it would be fair if Mr. Nicholls had a day, that I had a day to do a cross-examination. Of course, I will try, with the advantage of having heard what I heard, to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but no cross-examination takes the same length of time as the examination-in-chief. So let's start from there. Now that was the rule that was imposed on us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, it's the practice. In practice, the cross-examination usually doesn't last as long as the examination-in-chief. It depends. There are witnesses -- there are witnesses that, for example, Madam Baruch took twice as long.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: But this has now taken three times as long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, okay, but...

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And Your Honour, we -- unlike the Prosecution, you have given us a deadline date, when we have to finish with our witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: If they keep taking three times as long as we're taking, we're not going to get to put on the witnesses that we want to put on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman, but this witness will finish today. I can assure you. There's no way I can extend the testimony of this witness beyond today. That I am not prepared to do. But on the other hand, I -- with the exception of may be some questions which were less important than others, I don't think there's a case for us stopping Mr. Nicholls in the series of questions that he has been putting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, my request is this: That the Prosecution know in advance that there is a limit to the amount of time they can take on cross-examination because the entire cross-examination yesterday, Your Honour, almost every question dealt with matters that I had not raised at all on direct. I know that's not a rule. But it was things that you've already heard over and over and over just being repeated to you again. And it -- I mean, I really want to be able to put on the number of witnesses for Mr. Brdjanin that I think are important to be able to put on for him. But also, you've told me if I go past the end of January, I will be penalised in terms of the time I get to write my brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I never said you would be penalised, Mr. Ackerman. Don't put words in my mouth that I haven't said. In fact, yesterday, you remember well I said it's not going to be a big problem or the end of the world if we go beyond the end of January. You can find it --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I just want to really wind up the testimony in this case as early as possible because we do need, all of us, significant time to do the rest of the work that's necessary in this case. And cross-examinations that only keep showing you documents that you've seen over and over and asking the witness to say isn't that what it says, we had that today, just asked the witness isn't that what the document says, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He is an important witness. He is an important witness for the Defence, and he is also an important witness for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: May all the speakers please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I apologise. And he is being questioned on something which is fundamental to the case. He is one of those SDS members, actually a president of the SDS in his own community who became an outcast, who was ostracised, supposedly, by the SDS. And we are trying to find out exactly why. Because even your client at a certain time clashed with the SDS. So in our quest for the truth, Mr. Ackerman, we are trying -- we are trying not to be difficult with anyone. On the other hand, I do realise that you can't go on forever, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't intend to go on forever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I took your word yesterday before we quit, you said you will certainly finish today. And we are still here probably because you finished early, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: What he said yesterday was he thought he had a couple of hours of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what I understood, too. But in all honesty, I can't criticise Mr. Nicholls for the questions that he put to the witness today, starting with the intercept and also because these are two fundamental things. I mean, the role of Milankovic in the affairs happening in the region at the time, was he acting on his own or was he the instrument of someone else? That's number one. And secondly, also the Kozara. We started with the event, hearing testimony on the event a year and a half ago, if not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: May I respond. I'll be very brief, Your Honour. Your Honours are correct. There is no rule placed on them as to the length of their cross-examination. The Defence can't just limit the amount of information which the Court receives from a witness by ignoring whole areas. That's why the Rule 98 allows on cross-examination for a party to ask questions which are relevant to their case. Mr. Ackerman did that, and went into areas which he thought were important that we hadn't asked about. He has raised all of the issues, nothing I'm asking is beyond the scope, because he's tried to suggest that Veljko Milankovic was sanctioned and just looked at one document. He has tried to show that the association had a particular purpose and the evidence I suggest today that's coming out shows that that is not the case. And finally, when his witnesses are testifying, I don't stand up and object and comment and argue about what I think the documents are, but that eats up a lot of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now you are -- Mr. Nicholls, at the very end of it you try to spoil it and get Mr. Ackerman to stand up and object once again. Let's leave it at that. There is no hard and fast rule because we are all trained in these type of cases. We have to adjust ourselves to the circumstances that arise from witness to witness and from day to day and from minute to minute sometimes. So at the present moment the only rule is that there is is that you have to finish today. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: But when he asked questions like, "Could the ARK Crisis Staff command anybody?" "No." "Thank you." It's a little --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't have to preach that to any of us, Mr. Nicholls. We know what the rules are and I think Mr. Ackerman knows as well. And on that basis you can proceed. But please try to finish as early as you can. 20-minute break so that we try and finish before 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, although Your Honour I do want to raise the matters because of the time limit. I'd be grateful if you can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can raise the matter regarding the decision now if you want --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think we've had an hour and a half. The interpreters need a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's fair enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, you may proceed, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: April 1992, Veljko Milankovic attends and addresses a special session, extraordinary session, of the ARK Assembly. That same month, he gives an interview in which he states that he is a unit for and under the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Three years later on the anniversary of the takeover of the Kozara transmitter, he's praised in a newsclip. Kupresanin talks about how this was necessary, an armed takeover of the Kozara tower as part of the autonomous region's plan to separate, and there's a discussion about how they met with Milankovic at a restaurant in 1991 to plan the takeover of the transmitter. You still maintain your position that Milankovic and his men were not doing exactly as he said operating, as a unit for the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can answer yes or no or I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. No, you don't maintain your stance -- no he was not operating and he was lying in that interview, or no, you now change your mind and you concede that he was telling the truth when he said that he was operating under the Autonomous Region of Krajina's instruction?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not function under the Krajina region. What they were doing was illegal, and certain individuals who were with them, that was also illegal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I have no argument with you that what they were doing was illegal. Now, I want to move to another topic. It's something you talked about with Mr. Ackerman. You're an architect. Correct? That's your training?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You're not a lawyer? You've never been to law school?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You're no expert in constitutional law?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now, the -- you were asked a lot of questions about the Autonomous Region of Krajina, the ARK Assembly. And that's -- I want to just follow up on that. I can show you the document if you need it, but let me just see if you agree. Out of 196 members of the Krajina Autonomous Region Assembly, only about 6 were non-Serbs. If you don't know, that's all right.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: But you did agree yesterday that it was a Serbian initiative to a question put to you by His Honour, the Judge?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: My question referred not to the Autonomous Region of Krajina, but to the ZOBK.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I wasn't trying to confuse. And that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I meant to ask the same question with regard to the ARK, but later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When the ZOBK became the ARK, in essence, all that changed was the name. Correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to show you P95. This shouldn't take long because you've already looked at this document a couple times. These are the minutes of the 14 December 1991 ARK Assembly meeting which you attended and spoke at about Veljko Milankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's in the book that I prepared for him yesterday which is right there. It might be easier than dragging out all the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ackerman, for pointing that out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'd recommend that we keep the pages in the book and let him just use the book rather than taking the pages out. He'll get all mixed up, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you have those minutes in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If you look at the agenda for that meeting, number 2 is the current political and security situation in the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And that includes a report from the Security Services Centre and the security service of the 5th Corps of the JNA. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: There's not a single economic issue discussed at this session, is there?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: By yes, you mean there is not a single economic issue discussed. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, there is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Also, I notice, because we have the minutes of your conversation here, that you don't mention multiculturalism, pluralism, or creating a multiethnic society here, do you? It's okay. I'll withdraw the question so you don't have to read the whole document. If you want to answer, because I think it's apparent from the face of the document. This session -- go ahead.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to answer the question. May I make a comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If you're answering the question, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls is aspiring to become one of the Judges later on. Yes, answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vojo Kupresanin, the president of the assembly, called upon me to submit some kind of a report. That was unexpected. And you can see that this is not a report of the government; it is just an intervention on my part because I was not charged with submitting a report on behalf of the government because I was not the president of the government. I was, however, invited to the meeting, and I was caught unprepared. And you can see from this text that this was just a formal statement.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So the answer to my question is yes, you did not talk about creating a multiethnic society at this meeting, did you?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And like many sessions, and it increased, this one concerned the political and security situation in the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Correct? We've already talked about what was on the agenda.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember -- you've read the statute of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Correct? I think you were shown it yesterday --

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you recall what Article 16 is about?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is also in his book. He could refer to it if Mr. Nicholls would like him to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll read it out while you find it. Article 16: "The Autonomous Region of Krajina shall monitor the situation and coordinate activities for the organisation and implementation of preparations for All People's Defence in accordance with the law, municipal defence plans, and the republican defence plan." That was part of the role of the ARK. Correct? Article 16.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it now. But...

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, I know you're not a legal expert, but do you know that although there was a similar provision in the ZOBK Statute, that this was new to the association of municipalities historically, to their statute, this defence role?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that in the statute of the municipalities, there was something similar. Perhaps it was adopted from the statutes of the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's okay. You're not completely answering the question, but that's all right. My point is you'd agree with me that this is not a purely economic association; it has a defence role, a military role?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the level of the municipalities, that was as far as it went. They were not allowed to have more than that, even municipalities had certain leeway or certain freedom to establish -- to set up their own defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We're talking about the statute of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Correct, of the region?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This --

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Article 16 states that the Autonomous Region of Krajina shall monitor the situation and coordinate activities for the organisation and implementation of preparation for All People's Defence. Monitor and coordinate the activities. The last time: Do you agree with me that under this provision --

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: -- There was a military role at the regional level?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer specifically because the military role was something that belonged exclusively to the military, and the Territorial Defence and civil protection belonged to the municipalities. And we only took over those elements that belonged to the municipalities. And that is why I find it quite hard to answer your question. I'm sorry for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you understand what the Article Number 16 says?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you understand that this is the statute for the region?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you understand that it says that the role is to coordinate?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And prepare for All People's Defence?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you think that this is put in there just to -- for no reason whatsoever and has no effect? I know you're not a lawyer, but it doesn't seem like a very complicated provision to me.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me just ask you this, if you know - we don't need to go into it - do you know that on the 21st of November 1991 at the second session of the Assembly of the Serbian People, the decision was made to verify, to approve of the Autonomous Regions of Krajina, to legalise them? The autonomous regions, sorry. Not just of the Krajina, but just the autonomous regions.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm going to show you P118. This is an extract from the minutes of the 14th session of the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, from the 29th of February 1992. This was about the time that you were kicked out from your position in the Prnjavor SDS. Do you remember if you went to the 14th session? Do you remember, yes or no, if you attended that session?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't -- I'm not sure that I was at this session. I know that after the session of the assembly of the Serbian People in Sarajevo where I had some conflicts and some problems with the leadership, that after that I, in most cases, did not attend the sessions. I'm not sure, therefore.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. You've answered the question. Thank you. You're not sure. You might have remembered this one if you were there because it was pretty important. Radovan Karadzic was there, Krajisnik, Koljevic, Ostojic, and some of the top Serb leadership. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I probably did attend these, if there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, the agenda here, again, is the political and security situation of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's the first item on the agenda.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, let's just go straight to the conclusions. It should be towards the end. The deputies in the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina accepted the constitution of the Republic of the Serbian People of BH in full." Correct? That's conclusion number 1.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Conclusion number 2: "The status of the Autonomous Region of Krajina will be incorporated into the constitution of the Republic of the Serbian People of BH in accordance with its practical needs in order to achieve its free economic development."

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Number 3 -- now, you understand what both those conclusions mean, don't you? Those are pretty clear?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And number 3: "Establish immediately strict control of the territory of the Autonomous Region of Krajina."

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And that's pretty clear to you, too, isn't it, what that one refers to?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sessions like these, in practice, as far as I know how it looked like, if I may describe it, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd rather you didn't because it sounds like you're not answering the question. The question was: Do you understand what conclusion number 3 means, what its effect is, what that is about, as you understand the previous two?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. What was that conclusion? What was going to take place once that was passed? Let me start. That relates to the political and security situation, doesn't it? It's talking about taking control of the territory, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And that fits in actually perfectly with what Vojo Kupresanin said the purpose of the Autonomous Region of Krajina was in that videotape we saw earlier, doesn't it? He was talking about forming a state, and at the first step it was necessary to take this transmitter.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Kupresanin was saying that. But under this other item, that the Assembly of the Serbian People would determine the position of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, and it defines there how the government is set up, including the police and any other branch of government, thereby removing from the Krajina the right to have this kind of exercise, this kind of control. So this decision would be in contravention or already was in contravention of the decisions passed by the Assembly of the Serbian People and constitution. I don't know -- as far as I remember in February, the decisions and the constitution were already passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The top Serb leadership came down to this meeting, and at this meeting conclusion 3 was passed. Correct? At the ARK regional level, to establish immediately strict control of the territory of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Correct?
