utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me take you to P159. Just before we get to that, you've agreed with me that you remember the decision verifying the autonomous regions. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And making them -- in this conclusion we have been looking at, P118, the deputies of the ARK Krajina Assembly accept the constitution of the Republic of the Serbian People in full. That was conclusion number 1.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But whether it was in full, we don't know because the question is who was present at the session of the assembly. Anybody could come to the assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This session -- this conclusion is signed by Vojo Kupresanin, the president. Correct? It has got his name attesting to it.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And the secretary Boro Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: These regions were part of, integrated, and legalised into the Serb Republic and the Serb constitution?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can we go to 159, please. P159.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is an ARK Assembly decision on the formation of the special-purpose police detachment from 27th of April 1992. You have that in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And in fact, the news article we looked at earlier - I don't want to go back to it unless you need to be reminded - the article from April 1992 which spoke -- which talked about Veljko Milankovic speaking at the assembly also talked about how at this session an order was made to establish this special-purposes police detachment. Correct? That was reported in the press. Right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And in fact, this detachment came into being; this decision was acted upon and took effect. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You don't know whether there was a CSB, special detachment formed in Banja Luka in April 1992? Do you remember the parade to commemorate the event?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In that period of time, I did not take part in these meetings and sessions. But please believe me --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's not the question. I'm not ask whether you took part. The question is do you remember this being acted upon, the Banja Luka special unit was formed. You know that happened, don't you?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure that it was formed pursuant to this decision only, Mr. Prosecutor. I'm really not avoiding an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But do I take it that at the same time you are acknowledging and you are accepting that this unit was formed in April 1992, special detachment of the CSB?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The special detachment of the public security station was not under the authority -- or rather, it was not formed pursuant to this decision. It was established pursuant to the constitution and the ministry that had been established within the framework of the constitution and the existing laws as adopted by the Assembly of the Serbian People. Or rather, at that time, the Republika Srpska of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not seeing Mr. Ackerman or Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Again, you're not a lawyer. Right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You're not a lawyer. You haven't studied with law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's not argue. Leave it at that, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I just want to know what his basis is for thinking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: His basis is that he's contesting you on the authority under which this special detachment was created. So initially, in the beginning, he was not even acknowledging that there was such a thing. He said he didn't know or wasn't sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll ask one more question, if I may, on this, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, but not the same question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you agree that this special detachment was formed around this period? You remember the parade in May, you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No, no, he did not say he remembered the parade in May. You didn't give him a chance to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You suggested it was in April, and he seemed to take that, but he never mentioned May himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's true. Let's clear it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember the parade to commemorate the special detachment?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What is your basis -- you tell me what your basis is for saying that it was not pursuant to this order, your legal basis or your factual basis.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was convinced at the time. However, now I believe that all the power as far as the setting up of the police forces was concerned was within the hands of the Republika Srpska of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The relevant laws and regulations were passed. This document is illegal. All it can do is express support on the one hand, but I really can't state that anything was established pursuant to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You believe that the special detachment establishment -- the establishment of the special detachment was legal. Correct? It wasn't an illegal act?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I believe is entirely a different matter. What my views were on the laws that had been adopted by the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That's one thing. But this assembly and this government passed the laws that were imposed on Krajina and everyone else, and it did have a police ministry. Krajina was in no position to set up anything like that because it lacked the power to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And yet, this order is issued from the Krajina level, and the --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, it's not an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This decision is issued at the Krajina level and the special detachment is set up. Right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way I see it here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like you to look at P153. Now, this is a decision of the Serbian Republic Ministry of National Defence on the establishment of the Territorial Defence, the TO, as an army of the Serb Republic, 16th of April 1992. Right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If you look down under where it says decision the second time --

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: -- An administrative war is hereby declared. Correct? Sorry, a state of imminent threat of war is hereby declared. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And the prior decision number 1 states: "The Territorial Defence of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina shall be established an armed force of SBiH. Command and control of the TO will be exercised by municipal district and regional staffs and a republican staff." Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says. But may I just be allowed to clarify a point. Before there were the municipalities and the second instance, regional level of authority within the police, but make no mistake about this --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you here --

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: -- Because that has nothing to do with my question. This is an important document, an imminent threat of war, mobilisation of the TO. We've just gone over those decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that was a question. "Is this an important document?" I think was meant to be asked, or maybe there isn't a question yet. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I took it -- I'm still waiting for the question actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is an important document relating to the defence, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is addressed, among others, to the government of the autonomous regions and districts. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This, again, is a political and defence-related issue being put under their jurisdiction. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are organs established by the ministry. They're referred to here as regional, but they're under no jurisdiction whatsoever of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. This may be a very big mistake indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Forget whether it's a mistake or whether it's an act of wisdom. I mean, let's proceed with answering the questions that are put to you. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's what this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the word he used was not mistake. The word he used was confusion. There was a big confusion. And I think in all fairness, paragraph 1. Decision, Mr. Nicholls left out the last phrase of that. "The municipal district and regional staffs and republican staff of the SBiHTO," not like the autonomous region or the municipality. But it was the TO staffs that's referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You're not claiming this some kind of typo on this document, are you? Just to make sure I'm clear on that with you, when you talk about "confusion". You're not saying there's some kind of typing error on the face of this document, are you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He has got problems with interpretation. Mr. Vidic, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps you can explain to us what you meant when you said on the face of it, there seems to be some confusion here on this document. What were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant the following: The government of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina adopted laws governing the work of the ministry and defence. Within the framework of those laws, they also regulated the work of regional staffs. But still, it left within its own discretion for the ministers within the ministry that the regional staff should be answerable to them, and not that the Autonomous Region of Krajina should have any kind of command influence over them. This is the error that I was talking about in order to avoid confusion. It was not within the power of the Autonomous Region of Krajina to make these decisions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We've looked at a lot of documents here. The republic level accepted and verified the autonomous regions as part of the republic. Correct? You agreed to that.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: They were constitutional. You've agreed to that. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The government could act through these regions if it wished, which is why they had their own secretaries of defence. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ministry had its own lines of defence from top to bottom. But the Krajina did not. The ministry and the government made all the appointments from top to bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: They may have made the appointments, if -- you can argue that. However, the autonomous regions could be delegated the power to act and could act in their own defence. We saw that in the statute, didn't we?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the statute says, but this was never implemented. I know that it was never done. For example, the regional minister of the police was not answerable to Krajina, but rather to the ministry. The president, Vojo Kupresanin, Mr. Brdjanin, everyone who was a member of the government, they were merely puppets for the press. They made no appointments. They had no influence, not as far as the direct chain of command or military chain of command were concerned. That's as far as I understood the situation. If you study the documents more closely, maybe this could lead me to change my mind. But I'm telling you what I know. I know how this was done. It wasn't done in a serious manner. I know how decisions were adopted. Anyone wrote whatever they wished to. Mr. Boro Blagojevic would sometimes add things. You would never know at the next session what he had added. It was a comedy. Even my driver once took a decision, and I myself was chucked out of a session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You're saying all this and calling all these people and ARK officials puppets simply because you know they were responsible for a great deal of the crimes which occurred in the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Were they responsible or not? I don't know. They certainly were naive. They had no influence over anything. They were merely expressing their support for someone or other. They might as well have been just an ordinary association. That's at least the way it looked.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: An ordinary association which could -- you've agreed that Veljko Milankovic was a criminal and he took part in the ethnic cleansing of Lisnje. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We've seen documents and first-hand statements from Vojo Kupresanin, from Veljko Milankovic himself, and others that he was working under the direction of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were merely boasting about doing something. They never budged from their armchairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: These media puppets could call up, meet with, and control paramilitaries like Veljko Milankovic's?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. No. They had no power over that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: They were legalised by the republic level in these regions; they had their own statute; the statute called for defence; they sent out documents as one we've just looked at mobilising the TO. That was the legal chain which you do not accept. And on the other hand, they had their other means of power and direct contacts with these paramilitaries. Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, he has answered it maybe six times now. And asking it over and over is not is going to change the answer. Plus it's a very compound question. It has about six parts to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, let's play the game according to the established rules that we have used so far. You should have never said that the witness is not going to change his answer. That's what you actually said in the presence of the witness. Don't put the question again, Mr. Nicholls. Let's move to the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me show you P166.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not quarrelling with you, Mr. Ackerman; I'm quarrelling with your dentist.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is a dispatch to the chiefs of all public security stations from the Banja Luka Security Services Centre, 4th of May 1992. That's what you have in front of you. Right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It states: "We have received a dispatch from the government of the Autonomous Region of Bosanska Krajina in Banja Luka which we hereby forward to you in full." And this dispatch is from the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina Autonomous Region of Bosnian Krajina regional secretariat for national defence, signed by the secretary for the regional secretariat for national defence, Milorad Sajic. That's the order being forwarded. This actual document is signed by chief of the Banja Luka centre, Stojan Zupljanin. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The last line of Stojan Zupljanin's order states: "Chiefs of the public security station are personally responsible for the implementation of this decision. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is a mobilisation decision for the entire territory of the Autonomous Region of Krajina ordered by Milorad Sajic. Correct? That's item number 1 of the decision.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please read a bit slower.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. All these people, Stojan Zupljanin, Milorad Sajicic - I think it reads Sajicic - they were employed by the different bodies of the ministries. While I was there, I was not aware of Krajina or the Krajina government having a ministry of police or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This order from Sajic is in his capacity as the secretary of the regional secretariat for National Defence. Correct? That's where this order is coming from?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The secretary of the regional secretariat, I very much doubt that he was appointed by the Autonomous Region of Krajina. I would like to have a clarification on this, please. I'm not sure myself. I don't think he could have been appointed by the Autonomous Region of Krajina, but this certainly needs checking.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That wasn't the question. You don't need to answer questions which haven't been put to you. This is a real order with real effect at the Krajina level being distributed throughout the Krajina. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must ask this question: Who does this order come from? Who is Sajic or Sajicic?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You've never heard of Milorad Sajic?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. No. Really, I never have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls, let's go to the next.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You may not have been the best-informed person of what was going on in the Krajina region in 1992. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As concerns this specific period of time, I may not be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But if you aren't, what makes you doubt your ability to speak to us with authority on this period? Why are you so unsure? Why do you not consider yourself as best informed or well informed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the reason is that I know that throughout this period, all official appointments to positions of executive power were being made by the Republic of the Serbian People in Sarajevo. This is what I knew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How do you know that? What's your basis, please, for that statement? You don't know who Milorad Sajic is. You don't know what orders he made. How can you tell us who made all the decisions at the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Can he be allowed to answer the first question first, and then the second one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman is right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This date is the 4th of May 1992 when most of the laws were passed in connection with the functioning of the defence ministry and police ministry. And this is where the authority of Krajina ceases to exist. You can see this clearly, both in the constitution and in the relevant laws of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the time when the ARK Crisis Staff comes into being? So doesn't it look strange or sound strange or seem strange to you that at the same time you're saying that the ARK practically disappeared, for all intents and purposes, the same time one of the creations of the ARK, namely the ARK Crisis Staff, comes into being at the same time? It calls for an explanation from you. The ARK was a puppet --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The ARK and its components were puppets according to you. I would assume that the ZOBK before, perhaps, was also puppets at the higher degree. So now we move from the ARK to the crisis staff when you say that the ARK practically became unimportant. So what's happening in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As early as in January and February, it in fact began in December with the adoption of the constitution which was promulgated by the Assembly of the Serbian People in Sarajevo. For all practical purposes, the jurisdictions were defined there, and Krajina existed only pro forma. But in the laws on defence, which had been passed by that time, it was determined how the crisis staffs should be established in emergency situations. And I think that it also stipulated how war presidency would be established. And that is how the Autonomous Region of Krajina and its crisis staff, according to the constitution and the laws, was an extraneous body as far as its functioning was concerned. And the communication went from the ministry down to the municipalities. Krajina was just a puppet. It was there just for show. You can see that when you read the constitution and the laws passed by the Assembly of the Serbian People or by the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. According to these laws, everything was set up. Any police authority would be illegal for the crisis staff and the Autonomous Region of Krajina to assume would lead to conflict of jurisdictions. That is why Krajina and its crisis staff was used more in the media. It was presented to a greater extent in the media. It was quite clear to me that all the communications went up to Sarajevo, and the municipalities had direct communications with Sarajevo. Sarajevo established the regional levels of government according to its own laws, but it had nothing to do with the Autonomous Region of Krajina, and the crisis staff merely approved what had already -- or rubber-stamped what had already been decided elsewhere. Quite a few of the decisions passed by the crisis staff of the Krajina and the Autonomous Region of Krajina itself that were passed by them could not be implemented at the municipality level because the filter was there, and this is where the government actually functioned, at that level. I remember only one of the sessions of this kind. I was invited. I went there with my driver --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Session of what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. It was ridiculous. There was no protocol. There were no accreditations. Nobody knew who was invited. And because I did not agree with this kind of work, to work without the rules of procedure, and Mr. Brdjanin probably remembers that. He said, "Well, why are you bothered with that?" I know that I was quite literally thrown out of the session. It was held in a hall which was twice as small as this one here. I was kicked out, and my driver remained there, and he laughed later on saying that he, in fact, passed some of the decisions. It was quite ridiculous. I refused to go there any more because I couldn't do anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never had an opportunity to get things that had been adopted by the Krajina Assembly, by the regional board, at those -- by those institutions. Mr. Blagojevic, he drafted these documents later. We had quite a few disagreements about that, and I always strenuously protested. And that is why the validity of these documents was always in question because none of these documents was ever adopted at the next session. If you have a normal session of a government or any other kind of a session, item 1 on the agenda is always the adoption of all the written documents that were made at the previous session so that you can check what is it that had been adopted. I also have my doubts about the quorum, the required number of people. Many of such sessions, they were not there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't need to know now. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So thank you for telling us. You were thrown out of the Krajina Assembly as well as your local SDS presidency. Let me show you P285. This is the extract of the minutes of the 17 July 1992 Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Agenda item 4: "Verification of the decisions and conclusions adopted by the crisis staff and war presidency of the Autonomous Region of Krajina." If you look at item 4, you'll see the following debate. All decisions and conclusions adopted by the crisis staff and war presidency of the Autonomous Region of Krajina were verified by a vote of 98 to 1.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. But -- well, I wasn't present there in this period.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Look who was present. Momir Talic, Milan Martic, Bosnia-Herzegovina Minister of Defence Subotic, Bogdan Subotic, that is. Mr. Ostojic, members of the Republic government, members of the ARK, Krajina government. High-level military and political leaders taking part in this decision to verify all the decisions and conclusions of the ARK Crisis Staff. That's what this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is dated when?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: 17th of July 1992, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The other document which you showed the witness earlier which decision number 1 is to incorporate the status of the ARK, of the region, that is dated when?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll have to find that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it was 80 --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: 21st of November 1991, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have this document here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's not the one we're talking about. Do you have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just look at this document. I wanted to tie up the dates in order to understand better.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, do you remember my question?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters could not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Vidic, you said something which the interpreters couldn't catch. I heard you, but it didn't reach the interpreters' booth. Could you repeat what you said to Mr. Nicholls, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not understand the question. Could you please repeat it, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did this ARK Assembly session attended by the top political and military leadership, attended by representatives at the ARK level, the Republic level, all the decisions and conclusions of the ARK Crisis Staff are verified by a vote of 98 to 1, that's a pretty strong endorsement. Wouldn't you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Are these --

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- But I --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... decision for the media?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I have my doubts about the number of 99 councilmen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't worry about it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have my doubts about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't worry about it. For the moment, that's what we have anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Unless the witness has got first-hand information to contest what is contained in that declaration. But he wasn't there in any case. So Mr. Nicholls, I suggest you move to something different.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me show you P182. Pretty early ARK Crisis Staff decision, 9th of May 1992. The decision number 1 says that "all decisions and conclusions of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina are binding for all the municipalities." And we know that this decision was verified by those top leaders on the 17th of July 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, or perhaps this was illegal at the time. This was an illegal act, according to the laws and the way that they stipulated how government should be exercised.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think what you're starting to tell us is that in your view, the entire Serb Republic government structure, all the way up from the top, the presidency down, was illegal in your view in light of the constitution. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. That's not what I wanted to say. I wanted to say that this decision, first of all, is in violation of the statute of the Autonomous Region of Krajina; and secondly, which is even more serious, it is in violation of the constitution of the Serbian people of Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and its appropriate laws which concern jurisdiction, which were passed long time ago before the 9th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You may say it's illegal, but it was verified by the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I don't think there's any factual basis for that. There's no list of what the decisions were that they verified on the 17th. We have no idea what decisions were presented to them on the 17th of July that they verified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It states that they verified them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Who knows what "all" is? Boro Blagojevic could have put his own package in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All is all. When you say all decisions, it means all decisions, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In any case, Mr. Nicholls --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The thing is this, the witness is getting involved in legal pronunciations some of which are very delicate constitution nature which I am sure will be addressed at a higher level and not at this level.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's why I asked about his legal background, Your Honour. May I have P202, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, first of all, before we get to this, you will agree with me that the Muslim population, the Bosniak population, of Prnjavor was disarmed during the summer of 1992? They were told to surrender their weapons, right, to the police?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What you're looking at is a 20th of May 1992 Banja Luka Security Services Centre document --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He has got something else. Look at what's on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He has been given the wrong document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It should be P202.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, it says here -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You've got the wrong one, I think. I can give you my copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sir, I don't want to spend a lot of time on this because the Court has seen this document before. This has gone out to all chiefs, all departments, all police departments in the region, in the autonomous region, other than Jajce. It's signed or it's from Stojan Zupljanin. Read 23 -- paragraphs 23 -- just paragraph 23 to yourself, and the following paragraph which is not numbered.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I have only three paragraphs here, so I don't understand what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Usher, please. Show him this paragraph here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I wasn't given paragraph 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll read it out. "In all our activities we are obliged to observe all measures and apply all procedures ordered by the crisis staff of the autonomous region. With regard to disarmament, when the deadline for surrender expires on 11 May 1992, we should take no action until the crisis staff makes the relevant decisions. It is very important that we solve this problem comprehensively insisting on the disarmament of extremist groups." This is Stojan Zupljanin, head of the centre, making it clear to every policeman in the ARK region that they are to obey -- "observe all measures and apply all procedures ordered by the Crisis Staff of the autonomous region." Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Stojan Zupljanin was merely hiding behind the decisions taken by the Crisis Staff of the ARK. And he had jurisdiction -- or in fact, he was obliged to work in accordance with the laws and not in accordance with the political decisions in his police work.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: He is making an order based on ARK decisions saying ARK decisions must be observed. Correct? It's an order. He's not hiding behind anything.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, I'm not going to go through a long chain of documents that this Chamber has seen before, but will you agree with me that after May 11th, after the 14th of May deadline expired, that the police all throughout the ARK with the military began disarming Bosniaks and Croats?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to now have you take a look at P2608. I can give him my copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Here, here, here, here. I don't need this. That's the English text? And this is the one in his own language. Because I see that they are of equal...

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Have you ever seen this document before, the Official Gazette from your municipality?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, really, I haven't. I really haven't seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, that sort of explains a few things, I think. If you look at item number 38, conclusion 38, okay? Go to there, first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's the first page -- it's the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's actually only the first page in English, Your Honour, because the entire gazette has not been translated. It's page 7 in your B/C/S version, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Go to page 7, it has a number on the top that says 02949295. Number 38. Have you found that?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's a decision on the temporary confiscation of hunting weapons dated the 15th of May by the president of the crisis staff, Nemanja Vasic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: "This decision is being taken pursuant to item 5 of the decision of the Government of the Autonomous Region of Krajina number 01-1/92 dated the 4th of May 1992." Isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, but they passed the decisions they wanted to. Not all. The municipality implemented only those decisions that it liked. Not all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Have you done a survey of every municipality and every decision? Because before you were telling us you were telling us you weren't the best-informed person in the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I have to apologise to the Prosecution. I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you did not know that this decision was, in fact, implemented, did you, before now?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did know that this was implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This was one they did want to implement, disarming people. Go to number 42, please. I'm sorry. That's an interesting one about the expulsion of refugees. But because of the timing, let's go to number 43, the next one. This states: "At its 14th session held on the 23rd of June 1992 and on the basis of the conclusions of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina of 10 June 1992, the Crisis Staff of Prnjavor Municipality adopted the following decision on residence searches and confiscation of property." Again, relying on the ARK Crisis Staff, their authority, to implement this conclusion, correct, this decision?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that this is correct, but that was after I left, and I did not know about all these drastic things they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let's go to number 44, the very next one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls, we need to have a break. How much longer do you need to conclude?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think I'm going to fill up the session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I must have some time for redirect. He can't take all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is what I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How much time does he need for redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think probably half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Does the Chamber have questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: At least I can forget my questions. Can I ask the cooperation of the interpreters and everyone to have just a 15-minute break? No, I can't. Mr. Ackerman will have all the time he needs for his redirect. If the cross-examination has lasted so long, I can't... I need a feedback, because I can't see. Okay, so we'll have a 15-minute break now, and then I will direct both of you accordingly to make sure that we finish with the witness today.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime, see which questions you really need to ask before you bring your cross to an end, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can I know what my deadline is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman needs half an hour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the president, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think probably about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Could be a little less, a little more. It's hard to tell at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can I have until 6.30, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, no. Of course not. You need to conclude in 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Fifteen minutes, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think this chapter on the implementation by the Prnjavor... I think you can skip it. Because it's documented anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: There are some more, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He isn't going to enlighten us much more anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll abandon that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You said yesterday speaking with Mr. Ackerman, that the time you stopped -- I'll read exactly what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When did you officially end your membership in the party? This is on page 16.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some periods in which I was strongly opposed or when my views were very different from their views. It was in February 1991, and then in December, January, or February 1992. And in February or March of 1992, I did not attend the sessions of the main board at all, and also the sessions of the assembly until the fall of 1992. Is that right? So did you attend any assembly sessions in March 1992? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. Excuse me, if I may, Mr. Prosecutor, I said no too quickly. I think I misunderstood. Which assembly are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I meant all assembly, but instead of that, let's just go to the Assembly of the Serbian People on the 11th session in March of 1992. You were there. You spoke at length. This is P2474. Now, I don't know if I have enough time to go through every word of this, so I've highlighted some points for you to look at. You speak, and I'd like you to go to the third section. Well, because of the timing, let's go to number 4. Do you see where further on I've written the number 4 next to a highlighted section? It states: "The only road we can take is to make a confederation out of the BH to reach no agreements, to keep on buying time and negotiations, and to achieve something at the Belgrade level. "If that does not happen, there will be no war, true. There will be peace. The Serbs will lose everything. The worst possible scenario. I am much more afraid of peace than of war." That was your contribution to whether the problems should be solved by agreement or by violence. There's nothing in there about establishing a happy, pluralistic, multicultural society, is there?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I couldn't say what I really wanted to say within the framework of every single item on the agenda.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So you concentrated on the important points which was that you were in favour of war. I understand that. Look down at where I've highlighted number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Was that last part a question? Starting with "so you concentrated"? And if so, does he get to answer it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll withdraw it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Question withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Go to number 6, sir. "The status quo on the ground" - and I'm on page 39 of the English - "has to be taken in Banja Luka and in Serbian towns. And the question is how? We can do it by following certain rules, but not through chaos. That is why I propose that the local Krajina Assemblies should act as more extreme elements." Now, that kind of contradicts what you have been saying, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If you give it to me, I can find the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You're suggesting that the Krajina Assemblies, the Krajina Assemblies have an even more active role on the ground, in taking the ground. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This expression here, "more extreme," it is not what it appears to mean. My aim was for the association of municipalities to go officially into the assembly where the representatives of all the ethnic groups from a given area would take part, not only Serbs. Let me just check the context of this, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You can put this in context, too, that after your advocacy, that the Krajina assemblies should act as more extreme elements. "There are undoubtedly many concrete actions, concrete actions that can be taken. We also have methods for financing this, and all it takes."

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Listen, more extreme in terms of the way the authorities were functioning because in this shape, they had no power whatsoever. My idea was for this to evolve as some kind of autonomy, to go in that direction. This is no secret. But a multiethnic autonomy which would have the power of negotiating with the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the aim was to develop its own diplomacy. But the aim was to have a war, the grey eminences inside the government had paved the way for this. It was obvious. There were invisible, hidden centres of power who governed the entire thing. This expression "more extreme" did not mean that it had to be a Serb-only government. I know what the colour of my personal politics was at the time. I'm not saying that I felt no fear back then concerning the risk to my own life, the hostile environment that I lived in, the frustration that was felt among the people. Everyone felt this. The question was how to survive, how to protect yourself in those times. I felt this fear, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think you've explained that. Just last question on this document. Go to where I have highlighted number 1. It's right after you begin speaking. You start off by saying: "I would like to salute you all..." And then you say for the first time that you would not be pleased at least with any agreement, and you continue to state: "Why would I not be pleased if any agreement would be made in the BH? Not because I'm a hawk or because I want war. I'm trying to point out there are other Serbs in other places with whom we have to work to arrange things jointly. The problem with the remainder of this country is a problem with Serbs," and I think you mean just of the Serbs of Bosnia and Herzegovina. You kind of failed to mention there the problems facing non-Serbs again, don't you?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did fail to mention that at the time because this was a different subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now, the last part I want to cover with you very briefly, you stated yesterday to me that you were never involved in weapons smuggling. You maintain that. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Smuggling, no, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: During the wartime, at any time during the war, were you involved in any unlawful activity which could be considered profiteering from the wartime conditions?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But I was on a number of different occasions accused. I was being accused beyond belief whenever I failed to consent to agree with everything that was being done within the SDS. I was facing difficulty throughout the whole period of time, and then some of the accusations were made public, that I was involved in the obtaining of weapons, that I was working with the SDO, that everyone knew I had contacts in Belgrade, that I was a personal acquaintance of Mr. Dzindzic, or Mr. Peric who was a member of his board who is a friend of mine from my university days. Everyone knew that I had attended meetings of that party in Belgrade. However, there were certain circles who did not exactly like this and described me as SPO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay, I understand you're saying you were attacked because you weren't in line with the SDS by some people. My question is was one of the accusations placed against you that you were involved in actually running illegal, organised telephone communication with the people in the Republic of Croatia in 1994?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me show you P0032946. This is an RS Ministry of the Interior state security department centre, Banja Luka, strictly confidential information on illegal organised telephone communication in the Republic of Croatia, 16 November 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, my only concern is relevance. He has already indicated that yes he had been -- that there was an accusation made against him in that regard. What's the purpose? There's nothing to impeach here. He agreed that he had been accused and it's 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, in all fairness, I think I should let him read this document quickly. This is an act of dishonesty. He has only said that he was accused. I haven't asked him whether or not in this case -- whether in this case he did it, whether he's guilty of this crime against state security for profit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It goes directly to his credibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: In addition, Mr. Nicholls is 5 minutes past the time you allowed him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I'm pushing Mr. Nicholls to conclude it here, but the witness must answer this question. You've read the accusation that is directed against you in that document. Yes, your question now, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't know if we need a warning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Are you guilty of that offence? I don't know if that case is still open or pending against you. Were you diverting calls for profit to Croatia in violation of state security laws? And I've got one more document you might want to see before you answer. P0012794.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And that will be the last one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do wish to comment on this, if you want to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. But I think I should let you read this other very short document. This is the next day, 17 November 1994, stating, again, RS MUP, official note, stating that you appeared. You were at that time a deputy of the RS Assembly. And you came to the CRDB in Banja Luka and you wanted to talk to the officials there, the officers, about the issue and that you may have been imprudent when you joined the mobile phone business and asked what could be done. The only question I want you to answer is if it's true you were involved in an unlawful activity for profit as stated in this first document I showed you.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did do that, but that was no profit. There was an agreement between myself and other people in Croatia to set up a link and to make it possible for those people to speak to their families whom they hadn't heard of or from in years. This was not about mobile phones; this was about telephones.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So this was a crime committed out of charity, not because you were charging 6 DM a minute, as it states in the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It wasn't charging actually. They were being charged 6 and were getting 4. That's the allegation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's right. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You committed this crime out of the goodness of your heart, not because you were getting 4 DM a minute.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please allow me to tell you this: Mobile telephones and related expenditures at the time, I'm not sure how much a mobile phone in Croatia would have been charged, and the local telephone lines and so on and so forth. This entire service, it was merely about covering the expenses, and no one at all was obliged to pay. It was said at the beginning 4 Deutschemark. Whoever could pay simply paid up. But not too many people could actually afford to pay. But as soon as we started doing this, the police cracked down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can we close here, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, I think the document speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry, I need to just tender these as 2711 will be P00 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because I need to mark them. The first one which is dated 21st November.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry, 16 November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 16th November, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And the second one, 17 November is 2712.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 2712. Are you tendering the one dated 21st November?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That would be 2713.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have all the time you require.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Vidic, in your testimony yesterday at page 82 of the LiveNote, you were responding to one of Mr. Nicholls' questions, and you said this: "Brdjanin had a run-in with Mladjenovic regarding Milankovic." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: What -- tell the Chamber what you know about Brdjanin's run-in with Mladjenovic regarding Milankovic. What was that about?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic was a journalist, and he was a boastful person. He took photographs of himself. He made comments in the papers. He would bring Milankovic to Krajina, and everyone was sick of them coming there. There was a great deal of tension and disorder at the time. I know that Mr. Brdjanin complained, and as Mr. Brdjanin complained there was disagreement between Mr. Brdjanin and Miro Mladjenovic. I know that Mr. Brdjanin reacted vehemently, as he usually does, with a great deal of energy. He wanted those people to stop loitering about, to stop compromising Krajina's image and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: When you say "he wanted those people to stop loitering about" are you referring to Milankovic and his people?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mostly I was referring to Milankovic and his people.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And what was the dispute between Brdjanin and Mladjenovic as regards Milankovic? Why did Mladjenovic and Brdjanin have a dispute about Milankovic?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the extent that I understood this, Mr. Brdjanin refused to have an informal unit doing something, or rather in Krajina, in Croatia, moving about, throughout the area to start loitering about the assembly, to be in the way. I know there was disagreement over this. Secondly, I know that Mr. Boro Sendic, who is also in favour of Milankovic's people in that group, they were seen together and at the same time they were trying to hang about Krajina. This was impermissible. I shared this view. But Mr. Brdjanin was very much of the view that those two did not belong together. We were merely a municipality at that point. We had no jurisdiction over everything -- over anything. No power. We just had meetings that meant nothing at the time because there were no instruments for us to use. There were attempts to set up an association within the constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina, a legal association. At the very outset there were earnest attempts made to this effect. Despite the extremism manifested by certain individuals, this was only about the association.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm leaving him in your hands, Mr. Ackerman. Whenever you want to stop him, stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: This issue that Brdjanin had with Mladjenovic as regards Milankovic, do you have any memory of which side of that issue Vojo Kupresanin was on? Was he supporting Mladjenovic or was he supporting Brdjanin, or do you remember?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe he was supporting Brdjanin. Brdjanin, yes. Yeah, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'd now like you to - it's in your book - look at the document P0095. This is that meeting of the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina on 14 December 1991. If you look at the first paragraph, you'll see that that meeting started at 10.00 in the morning. I'm sorry, you haven't found it yet. P95. This is an extract from the minutes. This is not the full minutes, it's just an extract. You'll notice that the meeting started at 10.00 in the morning. And then if you look at the very last page, it's only a three-page extract, I believe, if you look at the very last page, you'll see that the session ended at 7.00 that night. In other words, it lasted for nine hours, did it?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And Mr. Nicholls, in his questions of you, said there was no discussion of any economic items during that meeting, was there? Can you be sure that in that nine-hour meeting, that you never discussed economic items, like under item 4 "other business" perhaps?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be sure. It was a long time ago. I can't remember. If it took such a long time, probably there was something else being discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. Let me have you look now at -- it's in your book. It's Exhibit P35. Mr. Nicholls talked about it as P118, but they're the same document. And this is the 29 February 1992 meeting. And that's the meeting that was attended by Karadzic, and you were asked about, under conclusions, paragraph 3, which read "establish immediately strict control of the territory of the Autonomous Region of Krajina." At the end of February 1992, what was going on in the Krajina that would have caused this group to want to exercise some control over the territory? Was there some out-of-control activity going on?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was widespread feeling that there was no control. There were three ethnic groups and three groups within those three ethnic groups. The Green Berets had been set up in the Muslim towns and cities, in the Croatian ones, the Croatian Defence council. They had already mobilised people and set up informal military forces. It was in the same period that they had disarmed the legal police forces in Bosanski Brod. There were grey centres of power at the time. Those were party armies. There was a risk of chaos where, for example, the majority population of one of the ethnic groups would get itself armed and start conflicts. The whole thing could have easily got out of control and consequences would have been unforeseeable. There were attempts to do something about it. There were different activities that were underway. I know that there was a good number of municipalities that wanted peace and this desire for peace would override everything else. People wanted safety. Everyone was happy when an armed group was disarmed. And immediately, there was order back in place. There was pressure from the public to bring back peace and order. You couldn't go anywhere any longer. There were roadblocks manned by armed people who were not particularly good at handling weapons. There was a danger that they would kill you just out of fear by a knee-jerk reaction. So yes, there had to be some form of authority. What sort of authority, that was the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Was this related in any way to the initiative to disarm the various paramilitaries like Milankovic's group and other similar groups? Was this paragraph related in any way to that?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This date here, 1992, I'm not quite sure whether this refers to that particular thing. I can't really answer you. I believe that this decision was just a formal decision to make certain things possible. I can't really say.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. Let me take you to another issue. You spoke very briefly about a session of the Autonomous Region of Krajina that you attended in the company of your driver. Was your driver a deputy in the ARK Assembly?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Was he sitting in the meeting with you?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you told the Chamber that you got thrown out of the meeting because you wouldn't go along with something and that your driver remained there. And I think you said your driver took part in a decision or something. Can you explain that in a little more detail.

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was invited. I don't know exactly what date it was, which session it was. I was invited to many such sessions, but I didn't go. I decided to go for once. Mr. Njezic - I didn't want to go alone because it was wartime - he was my driver. We went there. It was held in a small hall of the Banja Luka Municipality building. There were so few people there. The person I knew was the commander of the Banja Luka Corps, the late Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you want to know, Mr. Ackerman, whether it's true that his driver actually reported to him that he had voted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just confirm that yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Did your driver actually participate in something in the assembly? Did he vote or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did he tell you that he had voted actually? Because you were not present.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I entered the hall, the session began. It was chaired by Mr. Brdjanin --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please, please, answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You already told us the story when you were being asked questions by Mr. Nicholls. Mr. Ackerman only wants to know whether it's true that your driver later on, when he came out of the assembly after you had been chucked out, told you: "this is all a farce. I even took part in the voting."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He would tell me that story for years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. That's all we needed to know. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Did that cause you to have any kind of an impression about that body, cause you to arrive at any conclusions about that body, that incident?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And what was that? What did you conclude from that incident?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That it did not have any real jurisdiction, that it was there just pro forma, and that it served a certain purpose, that this was not a serious institution, and that this was done on purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So Boro had reported the vote was 24 to 1 in favour of something. One of those votes probably would have been your driver. Right?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I want you to look now at another document, P227. And it's not in that book. Yes. You should be looking at the Official Gazette of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Is that only in English?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We certainly have it in B/C/S somewhere, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: We certainly do. I can put it on the screen if the technicians are up to doing that rather quickly. I don't know that they are. Yes. We've got it on the screen now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I just have to switch to the right one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You'll see there now in your language on the screen, it's decision number 1 in the Official Gazette. And this is -- I'm just going to -- because of the time, I'm going to tell you what this is. This is the order of Milorad Sajic that Mr. Nicholls was showing you within that document from the police where Milorad Sajic is ordering mobilisation within the Autonomous Region of Krajina. And what I'm interested in having you look at is the first paragraph right at the top. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Ackerman, because you may have it on your screen but we don't have it on your screen, and I want to make sure that the witness has it on his screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I had it for a minute. What happened to it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It is on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: There.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's the language I'm interested in right there. Now, my only question about that is does that indicate to you on what authority that mobilisation issue was being promulgated? Was it on the authority of the ARK -- Autonomous Region of Krajina or was it on the authority of the Minister of Defence?

utterances.speaker: DOBRIVOJE VIDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to the Ministry of National Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Vidic, I thank you very much for your time and being here with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's all the questions I have of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Ackerman. Mr. Vidic, we've come to an end, to the conclusion of your testimony. And before you are escorted out of this courtroom by Madam Usher, on my own behalf, on behalf of Judge Janu and Judge Taya, on behalf of the Tribunal in general, I should like to thank you for having coming over to give testimony. You will be given all the assistance you require to enable you to return to your home as early as possible. Madam Usher will now escort you, and our last words to you we wish you a safe journey back home

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, for your patience and for having listened to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before we wind up for the day, I think it is my duty as Presiding Judge in this trial to officially thank the interpreters, the technicians, the rest of the staff, and the counsel for Defence and Prosecution for your cooperation without which this witness would still be with us tomorrow. I really appreciate that, and particularly -- particularly we appreciate the cooperation of the interpreters, as I said, and of the technical staff. Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply to say I'd ask for 15 minutes tomorrow morning before the next witness to deal with the matter arising from Rule 98.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, well, but I don't think it's...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, no, no. Absolutely not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Thank you, everyone. And we'll meet again tomorrow in this courtroom at 9.00. Please be informed, I am doing my best to try to shift to other courtrooms as much as I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
